q: What if there were no toilets?
a1: Poop and pee would make places smelly and spread germs.

q: Why do we have the sea and land?
a1: The Earth has high places that are land and low places filled with water.

q: Why does a magnifying glass make things big?
a1: The curved glass bends light so things look bigger.

q: Do elephants drink through their trunks?
a1: Not quite! An elephant fills its trunk with water. Then it squirts the water into its mouth.

q: How do train wheels stay on the track?
a1: Each train wheel has a lip on its inside edge. The lip keeps the wheel from sliding off.

q: Why do I grunt when I lift something heavy?
a1: Holding your breath tight helps your body push hard. When the air lets out, it makes a grunt.

q: Why do icicles drip?
a1: Sun or warm air melts the icicle a little. The water slides down to the tip and drops off.

q: What are ribs?
a1: Ribs are curvy bones that protect your heart and lungs.

q: Could a cheetah beat a car in a race?
a1: For a short run, a cheetah is as fast as a car.

q: Why is my hair black?
a1: A coloring called melanin gives hair its color, and families pass it down.

q: How big were dinosaur eggs?
a1: The biggest dinosaur eggs were about as big as a melon.

q: Why do we win and lose?
a1: In games, one person may finish first, and another is next.

q: How do arches made of blocks stay up?
a1: In an arch, each block pushes on the blocks next to it. They squeeze together and hold each other up.

q: Why doesn't my friend want to play with me today?
a1: Sometimes kids want a different game or some time by themselves. It does not mean they don't like you.

q: Why do goats climb on everything?
a1: Wild goats live on high mountains, so they climb well.

q: Why do we have to eat protein?
a1: Protein helps your muscles and body grow strong.

q: Do animals fart?
a1: Yes! Most mammals fart. Tiny germs in their tummies make gas.

q: Why do we get goosebumps?
a1: Tiny muscles pull on your hair roots when you are cold or scared.

q: Why do seals have flippers?
a1: Flippers help seals swim fast in the water.

q: How far away are the stars?
a1: Stars are super far, much farther than the sun. A rocket would need over a thousand years to reach one.

q: Why do I keep breathing when I'm not thinking about it?
a1: Your brain runs your breathing all by itself, even when you sleep.

q: How can I make a light spot dance on the wall with a mirror?
a1: A mirror bounces sunlight in a new direction. Tilt it a little, and the bright spot moves far.

q: Why are some kids adopted?
a1: Sometimes a child's first family can't look after them. Then another family adopts them.

q: Why do people have different shaped eyes?
a1: Eye shapes come from your family, like hair and noses do.

q: Why do people put up bird houses?
a1: A bird house gives birds a safe, dry place to nest.

q: Why do we get hungry?
a1: Your body uses up its energy, so your tummy asks for more food.

q: Why does my tummy feel funny on a swing?
a1: At the top, you start to fall, and your insides feel floaty.

q: Why are days long in summer and short in winter?
a1: The Earth is tilted. In summer, your side leans toward the sun, so days are long.

q: Why does pollen stick to everything?
a1: Lots of pollen is sticky or spiky, so it clings to bees.

q: Are frogs poisonous?
a1: Some bright frogs are poisonous, but most frogs are not.

q: Do I have to eat my crusts?
a1: Crusts are just as good to eat as the rest.

q: Why do sweaters get little fuzz balls?
a1: Rubbing pulls tiny hairs out of the sweater. They twist together into little fuzz balls.

q: Why do grown-ups worry so much?
a1: Grown-ups worry because they care and want to keep people safe.

q: What is a forest?
a1: A forest is a big place with lots of trees growing together.

q: Why is a violin played with a bow?
a1: The bow's hairs grab the string and keep it shaking.

q: Why does bread have little holes inside?
a1: Yeast makes gas bubbles in the dough, and baking sets them.

q: Why do bubbles float?
a1: A bubble is a thin soap skin around air. It is so light that a breeze carries it.

q: Why does a raft float even with people on it?
a1: A raft is made of wood or air tubes, which float. The water pushes up hard enough to hold people.

q: What is nectar?
a1: Nectar is a sweet juice that flowers make deep inside.

q: Why do we write on lines?
a1: Lines keep letters the same size and in a straight row.

q: Why can hot water crack a cold glass?
a1: The inside of the glass heats and grows fast. The outside stays cold, so the glass pulls apart and cracks.

q: Why do cats stare?
a1: Cats watch things closely, like a hunter. They may see or hear a tiny bug.

q: Why do cows chew all the time?
a1: Cows bring swallowed grass back up to chew again. This is called chewing cud.

q: Why are ceilings usually white?
a1: White bounces light around the room. That makes the room look brighter and bigger.

q: What makes a good sorry?
a1: A good sorry says what you did and that you feel bad. Then it says how you will fix it.

q: Why are snail shells curly?
a1: The shell grows at the open end and curls around.

q: Why do I sneeze so much when I have a cold?
a1: Cold germs make your nose itchy and full of snot.

q: Is the sun on fire?
a1: Not like a campfire. The sun does not need wood or air like a fire does.

q: Why do we get wrinkly fingers in the bath?
a1: Your skin wrinkles in water, which may help you grip wet things.

q: Why do balloons shrink after a few days?
a1: The air or helium slowly sneaks out of the balloon. Less gas inside means a smaller balloon.

q: Why is my nose so runny when I'm sick?
a1: Your nose makes extra snot to wash the cold germs out.

q: Why do cats hiss?
a1: A hiss means back off! The cat feels scared or cross.

q: How do astronauts breathe in space?
a1: The spaceship carries air inside, like a sealed bubble. Machines clean the air and make new air from water.

q: Why do mosquitoes bite?
a1: Mosquitoes bite to get a tiny drink of blood.

q: How can I do things without thinking?
a1: After lots of tries, your brain can do a thing alone. Walking and riding a bike are like that.

q: How do baby sea turtles find the sea?
a1: Baby turtles crawl toward the brightest sky, which is over the water.

q: Why do dogs turn around before lying down?
a1: Turning in circles makes a cozy round bed. Wild dogs did it to flatten grass.

q: Why do some families have lots of kids?
a1: Some families want lots of kids, and some want one or two.

q: What is a flag?
a1: A flag is a cloth with colours that stands for a place.

q: Why do grass stains turn clothes green?
a1: Grass juice is full of green color. It soaks into cloth.
